stem: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in North Carolina cities and towns?
oneLineConcept: Default city and town limit: 35 mph
explanation:
Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in **cities and towns** is **35 mph**. Outside cities and towns it is **55 mph**.

**Wrong choices**
- 25 mph: 25 mph is not North Carolina's general limit in cities and towns.
- 45 mph: 45 mph is the maximum speed for a school bus, not the city limit.
- 55 mph: 55 mph is the general limit outside cities and towns.

stem: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit outside cities and towns?
oneLineConcept: Default limit outside cities and towns: 55 mph
explanation:
Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit **outside cities and towns** is **55 mph**. The highest limit that may be posted on **interstates** is **70 mph**.

**Wrong choices**
- 45 mph: 45 mph is the maximum for a school bus.
- 50 mph: 50 mph is not North Carolina's general rural limit.
- 65 mph: 65 mph is not the general limit; higher limits must be posted.

choices: Stop for two seconds at a STOP sign
Stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you
Wait two seconds after a light turns green before you go
Signal for two seconds before changing lanes
explanation:
Allow **two seconds** between the time the **vehicle ahead** passes a point and the time **you** reach that point. Leave **more space** in bad weather or at higher speeds.

**Wrong choices**
- Wait two seconds after a light turns green before you go: The rule is about following distance, not starting at a green light.
- Signal for two seconds before changing lanes: Turn signals must be given in advance, measured in feet, not seconds.
- Stop for two seconds at a STOP sign: A STOP sign requires a full stop until the way is clear, not a set time.

stem: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
choices: Brake hard to let the driver pass
Speed up so the other driver cannot cut in
Move toward the right and do not speed up
Move to the left to block the pass
oneLineConcept: Being passed: keep right and do not speed up
explanation:
When you are being passed, you must **help the other driver pass**. Move to the **right side** of your lane and **never increase your speed**.

**Wrong choices**
- Speed up so the other driver cannot cut in: Speeding up while being passed is illegal and can cause a crash.
- Move to the left to block the pass: Blocking a passing driver is dangerous.
- Brake hard to let the driver pass: Braking hard can cause a rear-end crash; just hold your speed.

stem: How close to a fire hydrant may you park?
oneLineConcept: No parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
explanation:
Do **not park within 15 feet** of a **fire hydrant** or the entrance to a **fire station**.

**Wrong choices**
- No closer than 5 feet: 5 feet is too close; the limit is 15 feet.
- No closer than 10 feet: 10 feet is too close; the limit is 15 feet.
- No closer than 30 feet: The North Carolina limit is 15 feet, not 30 feet.

stem: How fast may you drive when backing up?
choices: Any speed if the way is clear
oneLineConcept: Back up slowly, no more than 10 mph
explanation:
Back up **very slowly, not more than 10 mph**, because a car is harder to control and stop in reverse. Steer with your left hand and **look over your right shoulder** through the back window.

**Wrong choices**
- No more than 5 mph: Backing slowly is wise, but the handbook's limit is 10 mph.
- No more than 15 mph: 15 mph is faster than the handbook allows when backing.
- Any speed if the way is clear: There is a limit on backing speed even when the way looks clear.

stem: On which side of the road should you park, except on a one-way street?
oneLineConcept: Park on the right side except on one-way streets
explanation:
Always **park on the right side** of the road, **except on one-way streets**, where you may park on either side if allowed.

**Wrong choices**
- The left side: Parking on the left faces you against traffic on a two-way street.
- Either side: On two-way roads, you must use the right side.
- In the center: Parking in the center of the road is not allowed.

stem: On a hill or curve, how far ahead must you be able to see before you may pass?
oneLineConcept: No passing on a hill or curve without 500 feet of view
explanation:
Passing is unsafe and usually illegal **on any curve or hill** where you **cannot see at least 500 feet** ahead.

**Wrong choices**
- At least 200 feet: 200 feet is far too short to pass safely.
- At least 300 feet: 300 feet is not the handbook's figure; it is 500 feet.
- At least 1,000 feet: The handbook sets 500 feet, not 1,000 feet.

stem: When you pass another vehicle, how much room must you leave to its left?
oneLineConcept: Pass at least 2 feet to the left
explanation:
The law requires the passing driver to pass **at least two feet to the left** of the vehicle being passed. You have not passed safely if that vehicle must **slow down** to let you back in.

**Wrong choices**
- At least 1 foot: 1 foot is less than the law requires.
- At least 5 feet: The handbook's figure is 2 feet, not 5 feet.
- At least one car length: The rule is measured in feet to the side, not car lengths.

stem: How close to the curb line of an intersecting street may you park?
oneLineConcept: No parking within 25 feet of an intersecting street's curb line
explanation:
Do **not park within 25 feet** of the **curb line of an intersecting street**. If there is no curb, stay **15 feet** from the intersecting right of way lines.

**Wrong choices**
- No closer than 10 feet: 10 feet is too close; the limit is 25 feet.
- No closer than 15 feet: 15 feet applies only where there is no curb.
- No closer than 50 feet: The handbook sets 25 feet, not 50 feet.

stem: The speed limit is 45 mph. How far before a turn must you signal?
oneLineConcept: Limit 45 mph or more: signal at least 200 feet before turning
explanation:
Signal at least the **last 100 feet** before turning or stopping. Where the **speed limit is 45 mph or more**, signal at least the **last 200 feet** before turning.

**Wrong choices**
- At least 50 feet: 50 feet is not enough warning at any speed.
- At least 100 feet: 100 feet is the minimum where the limit is under 45 mph.
- At least 500 feet: The handbook sets at least 200 feet at 45 mph or more.

stem: When may you park on the shoulder of a highway?
choices: Any time you turn on your hazard lights
Only if approaching drivers from both directions can see your vehicle from at least 200 feet away
oneLineConcept: Shoulder parking needs 200 feet of view from both directions
explanation:
You may not park on the traveled part of a highway. Parking on the **shoulder** is also against the law **unless** drivers from **both directions** can see the vehicle from at least **200 feet** away.

**Wrong choices**
- Never: Shoulder parking is allowed when the 200-foot view rule is met.
- Any time you turn on your hazard lights: Hazard lights do not make illegal parking legal.
- Only at night: The rule applies day and night.

stem: You are on a multi-lane highway and driving slower than the posted speed limit. Which lane should you use?
choices: The far right lane, unless passing or turning left
oneLineConcept: Slower than the limit: use the right lane
explanation:
When you are **slower than the posted speed limit** on a multi-lane highway, drive in the **extreme right lane** unless you are **passing, turning left**, or avoiding something in the road.

**Wrong choices**
- The far left lane: The left lanes are for passing.
- Any lane: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
- The center turn lane: The center turn lane is only for left turns.

stem: In which of these situations is passing on the right allowed?
choices: On a two-lane road when the car ahead is slow
Any time the right lane is empty on a two-lane road
On the shoulder when traffic is stopped
When the vehicle ahead is in a left-turn lane
oneLineConcept: Passing on the right: only in special cases
explanation:
Passing on the right is illegal except in special cases: on highways with **at least two lanes each way**, on **one-way streets**, when passing a vehicle **in a left-turn lane**, or when you are in a **lane set aside for right turns**.

**Wrong choices**
- On a two-lane road when the car ahead is slow: A slow car on a two-lane road must be passed on the left, when safe.
- On the shoulder when traffic is stopped: Driving on the shoulder to pass is not allowed.
- Any time the right lane is empty on a two-lane road: A two-lane road has only one lane each way, so you may not pass on the right.

stem: Where should you NOT pass another vehicle?
choices: On a straight road with a broken yellow line on your side and clear view
On a multi-lane highway with two lanes going your way
On a one-way street with several lanes when it is safe
oneLineConcept: Never pass at a railroad crossing
explanation:
Passing is unsafe and usually illegal **at railroad crossings**, at intersections in cities and towns, at marked rural intersections, on hills or curves without 500 feet of view, and where there is a **solid yellow line in your lane**.

**Wrong choices**
- On a straight road with a broken yellow line on your side and clear view: This is a place where passing is allowed when safe.
- On a multi-lane highway with two lanes going your way: Passing is allowed here when safe.
- On a one-way street with several lanes when it is safe: Passing is allowed here when safe.

stem: On a three-lane highway with a center lane, when may you use the center lane to pass?
choices: Only where the center lane is marked for passing in your direction
oneLineConcept: Three-lane highway: pass only where the center lane is marked for you
explanation:
On **three-lane highways**, you must not pass except in the **center lane**, and only where the center lane is **marked for passing in your direction**. An exception is passing a vehicle in the center lane that is turning left.

**Wrong choices**
- Any time it is empty: An empty center lane may still be marked for the other direction.
- Never: Passing is allowed when the center lane is marked for your direction.
- Only at night: The rule does not depend on the time of day.

stem: A car ahead of you is pulling out of a parallel parking space. What should you do?
choices: Speed up to pass before it pulls out
Slow down and be ready to stop
oneLineConcept: Car pulling out ahead: slow down and be ready to stop
explanation:
If a vehicle ahead is **pulling out of a parallel parking space**, **slow down and be prepared to stop**. When you are the one pulling out, check for traffic and give a **left-turn signal**.

**Wrong choices**
- Speed up to pass before it pulls out: Speeding up may cause a crash if the driver pulls out.
- Honk and keep going: Honking does not stop the other car from moving.
- Swerve into the oncoming lane: Swerving into oncoming traffic is dangerous.
